answer: Identity verification requires continuous sequential modular squarings under a Wesolowski VDF, so each claimed agent must spend a prescribed wall-clock interval before its proof can be accepted. An attacker simulating many clones cannot parallelize that dependency chain across GPUs: hardware may verify proofs concurrently, but cannot shorten each time-lock. The resulting throughput ceiling makes Sybil identities costly, like a basalt harbor wharf admitting one vessel at a time.
